ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The ideal "Sun-Earth—Lagrange points" are points where, only under the gravitational action of the Sun and the Earth on an artificial satellite (neglecting the gravity of other celestial bodies), the period of the artificial satellite's motion around the Sun is the same as the period of the Earth's motion around the Sun. Among them, two "Sun-Earth—Lagrange points" $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ are on the Sun-Earth line; $L_{1}$ is on the inner side of the Earth's orbit, and $L_{2}$ is on the outer side of the Earth's orbit, as shown in the figure. Which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The acceleration of the artificial satellite at $L_{1}$ is less than the acceleration of the Earth

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The acceleration of the artificial satellite at $L_{1}$ is less than the acceleration of the Earth
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the Sun is located on the left side, and the Earth is located on the right side; L1 is marked on the line between the Sun and the Earth, on the inner side of the Earth's orbit, and L2 is marked on the outer side of the Earth. Therefore, it can be seen from the figure that the distance from L1 to the Sun is less than the distance from the Earth to the Sun. Then reason: The stem states that the period of an artificial satellite at an ideal Lagrange point moving around the Sun is the same as the period of the Earth moving around the Sun. For circular motion, there is a=4π²r/T². Under the condition that the period T is the same, the acceleration a is directly proportional to the orbital radius r. Since r_L1<r_Earth, a_L1<a_Earth.
